These adjustments control the gain setting of the analog amplifiers in the scanner hardware. The gain settings of these amplifiers determine the exposure of the Red, Green and Blue channels.
The software normally determines these settings without user interaction. However when you have a film that has extreme conditions such as over or under exposure,
there is a chance to produce better scan result by changing these settings manually.  Please note that use of this control may provide unexpected results.
The units are displayed in EV (Exposure Value).
To view the results of this adjustment, please press the "Redraw" button. A simulated result will be displayed in both the "Natural" and "Processed" preview screens.
Please push "Large" or "Precise" button until the pushing board of FD attachment appears.
After putting on or off an attachment, please push an "Eject" button.
In the normal (1X Sampling) mode, image data is taken directly from the 14bit A/D converter.
In multisample mode, successive identical scans are combined to reduce the CCD noise level.
This results in longer scanning times. To view the results of this adjustment a new preview
Note that there is a check box called "Settings to be applied to preview / Multi Sampling"
in the "Preview Settings" in the Preferences. Result will not be seen until you have turned
on this function. (Factory default is off)
If you turn on "Super Fine Scan" check box, the scanner will scan using only one
line of the three line CCD. Please be advised that this mode may reduce streaking
only when you have applied an extreme contrast enhancement. The scanning time will
become approximately three times longer than the normal scan mode.
Auto focus when film is inserted
The "Auto focus when film is inserted" is the default setting,
so that as soon as a holder (one of FH-835M, FH-835S, FH-869M, FH-869GR, FH-816 or FH-8G1)
is inserted into the SUPER COOLSCAN 8000 ED, the scanner will immediately perform an auto focus operation
for the first frame of the film. When you press the preview or the scan button in this case,
the scanner will not perform an additional auto focus operation. If you would prefer to
perform an auto focus at the time you press the preview or the scan button, please turn this
check box off. Please also refer to the "auto focus" check boxes that are located in three
different tab pages in the preference setting for the "Single Scans", "Batch Scans" and
When you press the "Calibrate" button, a scanner calibration is performed. The scanner calibration is automatically performed any time the film is changed.
If you do not change the film for a long period of time, and if the scanner environment, such as room temperature, is changing rapidly, the scanner calibration may drift.
This may result in banding noise on the scanned image. Please press the calibration button if you notice this phenomenon and then rescan your image.

CleanImage automatically fixes defects on the film surface, such as scratches and/or dust. As a result of this process, the scanning speed will be slower. If the resulting scans look soft, try the "Sharpen" mode.
This function incorporates Digital ICE(TM) technology developed by Applied Science Fiction Inc. (ICE=Image Correction Enhancement)
This control allows manual adjustment of the focus setting. This may be helpful if you are attempting to scan film that is warped.
NOTE: You will need to perform a new preview scan in order to observe the results of the change in focus setting.
This is the setting to specify a duration by the minute before the scanner begins to eject an inserted film.
This timer is reset whenever you operate the scanner to perform autofocus, thumbnail scan, preview scan and final scan.
Note: The calibration function has been chosen. While it is performed, the LED indicator on the scanner will blink. During this time, your mouse and keyboard will not respond.
The calibration will take 2 minutes to complete. Do you want to proceed?
The film has been rewound due to inactivity. Do you want to reload it?
The scanner does not appear to be powered on. Please make sure that it is connected to an AC power source and is switched on, then try again.
The scanner has reported a hardware error. Please reset the scanner by switching on and off. If this does not work, please contact your local Nikon Service or Support office.
The scanner reports that the autofocus has failed. Hold down the "Control" key and press the autofocus button on the screen, then click to select a new focus area in the preview window.
The scanner could not load the film. Please consult your user's manual.
The stage locking screw is still in place. Please remove it.
Please remove the film holder and press the "OK" button on screen to try again.
There is no film in the scanner.
Please place film in the loader and press the "Feed"  button on the screen.
The scanner has reported that it could not load the film. If there is film in the scanner and it has failed to load, please consult your user's manual.
The crop area that you have selected is too small. Please make it larger.
Please remove the film holder and press the "OK" button on screen to try again.
The film will be rewound before calibration. Do you want to proceed?
The scanner has detected more than 6 frames on the strip film. To scan film of more than 6 frames, the SA-30 Spool Unit accessory is required.
The number of frames on the film strip is too few or too many. The film strip should have more than 2 frames and less than 6 frames for the SA-21, or less than 40 frames for the SA-30.
The scanner has reported that it could not load the film. The film may be too short or too long.

The scanner could not eject the film. Please press the "OK" button to unlock the adapter and  remove it from the scanner, then remove the film from the adapter. Please consult your user's manual for information.
Could not find the selected frame on the film strip.
This scanner does not support the adapter that is currently inserted. Please consult your user's manual for a list of supported adapters.
A data transfer error has been detected. Please try again. Note that another device on the same interface (1394 OR USB) may be the cause of the problem.
The film adapter may be loose. Please make sure that it is correctly inserted.
Please eject the film before you attempt to change the film adapter. Please return the adapter back to the original position.
The scanner has reported problem with the firmware. Please download the latest firmware from the list of Nikon Technical Support web sites or contact your local Nikon Service or Support office.
An error has occurred while executing a command.
Make sure that the holder slot cover is completely open.
Install the supplied black mask when using the FH-869GR glass holder. The scanner has detected that the mask is not in place.

The scanner has detected an Unknown film holder model. Make sure the square holes located at the front end of the film holder are clear. If this message appears again, try another holder. If this message still appears, please contact Nikon service.
The autofocus operation has failed. To manually select a point on which to focus. hold down the Control key and press the autofocus button. Then click on the desired point in the preview image.
